title: Local Services SaaS
subtitle: Build recurring revenue without drowning in onboarding, collections, and support.
description: Serve fragmented local operators with visible pain, tight budgets, seasonal demand, and uneven digital readiness. Revenue can arrive early, but finite market reach, late payment, disputes, bad debt, high-touch onboarding, and founder support can erase margin and hide churn risk.
learningObjectives: Distinguish software retention from founder service
Manage receivable aging and collection trade-offs

problems.title: Every prospect describes a different workflow
problems.summary: The market is accessible but may be too heterogeneous for one product.
hypotheses: One trade has repeatable scheduling pain
Payment collection is the shared bottleneck
The market is too fragmented for SaaS

problems.title: Manual onboarding may erase gross margin
problems.summary: Each account needs imports, configuration, and founder training.
hypotheses: A template can eliminate most setup
The customer should pay an onboarding fee
The product targets the wrong system of record

problems.title: Interest disappears when price is discussed
problems.summary: Usage interest is not yet backed by credible budget evidence.
hypotheses: The buyer expects a consumer price
The workflow is annoying but not costly

problems.title: Founder support is becoming the product
problems.summary: High-touch help creates retention while hiding standalone software value.
hypotheses: The founder is overpromising custom workflows
